title: SEBI, RBI work on bond indices, faster FPI onboarding - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Mumbai: Securities and Exchange Board of India Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey and National Stock Exchange of India Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Ashishkumar Chauhan during the 3rd Annual Conference of the Association of Portfolio Managers in India , in Mumbai, on Wednesday | Photo Credit: PTI

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) are working on a framework to enable trading in bond indices and associated derivatives, while jointly working to cut the time taken by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to enter the Indian market, SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Wednesday.

“One of the points that we are working on is bond indices… how we can have bond indices trading on exchanges,” Pandey said on the sidelines of the third annual conference of the Association of Portfolio Managers in India (APMI). “I believe the RBI has prepared some draft guidelines and asked for comments, and we are pursuing with RBI to finalise,” he said.

The regulators have been working in closer coordination on easing access for foreign investors and to make the process fast, seamless and digital. “There is much more active interregulatory coordination…on FPI onboarding, SEBI and RBI are currently engaged very actively on ironing out many issues. We have already achieved quite a lot but our ambition is more. We want to make it further simple.”

The regulator has already tested, with the help of depositories and custodians, cutting the onboarding timeline of about five days, compared with processes that can take more than a month.

As part of the digital push, SEBI has also moved towards digital signatures, e-Power of Attorney, a common application portal and tracking mechanisms, reducing reliance on physical documents, notarisation and apostille requirements.

Pandey said the RBI is also looking at allowing certification of FPI registration documents by foreign commercial banks and using the SWIFT network to transmit the certification.

The measures are part of a broader effort to reduce the time and paperwork involved in bringing foreign capital into Indian markets. Pandey said investors would ultimately decide where to allocate capital, while regulators' role was to make market access easier.

The regulator has been seeking to improve liquidity and participation in the corporate bond market. SEBI is also working on a market-making framework covering liquidity, market infrastructure and repo access, besides proposals for Fixed Income Channel Partners to expand distribution through regulated online bond platforms.

Pandey also clarified that SEBI has not formed any committee to examine allowing stock exchanges to trade their own shares on their platforms, including through the “permitted to trade” route. The clarification follows reports that the regulator was considering a panel on self-listing rules.

Speaking at the conclave, Pandey said SEBI’s focus would increasingly be on simplifying regulation while expanding investment options. He said the next phase of market development would require greater use of technology, but accountability for investment decisions must remain with identifiable human decision-makers

The SEBI chief said there is scope for the PMS industry to expand at a faster pace, at over 20 per cent. The assets under management in the PMS industry has reached around ₹9.2 lakh crore by August 2026, from around ₹1.4 lakh crore at the end of FY16, suggesting a growth of 20 per cent annually.
